target_customer: Social teams at brands and publishers
problem: Standing out in the Facebook News Feed is hard; teams wanted to test how videos, articles and images appear and publish the winner.
product_category: Social media A/B testing and publishing

technical_complexity.rationale: Posting variants through the Facebook API and measuring engagement is straightforward engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Entirely dependent on Facebook's API and ad tools, easy to copy, no lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources found; the cause of shutdown is not public.

market_need_then: Facebook organic reach was declining in 2014 per the company's own site copy; no further demand evidence found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Marketing copy: 'Testing is every top social team's secret weapon'

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Naytev was a three-person S14 company selling Facebook A/B testing. YC lists it as inactive, but no shutdown announcement, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public; platform dependency on Facebook and a narrow product are plausible risks but are not stated by any source and are not coded.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: StartupIntros reports a $1M seed in Oct 2014 (single source); PitchBook shows a $120K accelerator deal Aug 2014 and a $3.42M total. None recorded as rounds. No dated competitor sources found. Shutdown date unknown. Crunchbase page was placeholder text.
